theory: The application translates operator choices and machine configuration into assembled mathematical workflows. Terminal rendering and asynchronous questions are ports, while wiring chooses concrete runtimes and tools. Setup failures are operator-visible states rather than proof outcomes.
instead_of: Treating the CLI as the application core would combine construction and interaction; the Ui port and runtime factory instead support multiple surfaces over workflow owners.

absorption.rationale: Additional commands, another UI, and another runtime selection have clear homes in the registry, UI protocol, and composition factory.

world_mapping.rationale: Operator prompts, UI state, and runtime assembly correspond to distinct concerns; the UI explicitly represents event-loop responsiveness requirements.

abstraction.rationale: The UI seam is explicit, but State exposes config/session as Any and runtime construction forwards arbitrary context. Handler and factory requirements remain less discoverable than the Ui protocol.

justification.rationale: Async prompts are justified by deadlock, reopening is supplied through composition, and a test fences prompt_toolkit imports.

honest_limits.rationale: Wiring states SDK versus Hardy loop ownership and preserves unavailable setup identity as a recorded failure path.

rehearsals.why: The registry accepts handlers and user templates while protecting built-ins.

rehearsals.requirement: Offer operator questions through another asynchronous interface.
rehearsals.why: Implement Ui's awaitable choice and confirmation operations without importing the terminal renderer into handlers.

rehearsals.requirement: Select a third runtime from configuration.
rehearsals.why: Add an explicit composition-factory choice; the current branch is the intended construction home, although arbitrary context forwarding needs adapter tests.
